rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to explain ناشئة as one who rises, in Abyssinian usage.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق، عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس: نشأ: قام بالحبشة

rows.speaker: عمر، وابن عباس، وابن الزبير
rows.claim: They understand the night’s ناشئة to encompass the whole night; others likewise use it for rising at night.
rows.anchor: وقال عمر، وابن عباس، وابن الزبير: الليل كله ناشئة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: In another report Mujahid specifies the time after the night prayer; Abu Majliz, Qatada, Salim, Abu Hazim, and Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir agree.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية عن مجاهد: بعد العشاء. وكذا قال أبو مجلز، وقتادة، وسالم وأبو حازم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir synthesizes ناشئة الليل as the night’s hours and moments, each hour being called a ناشئة.
rows.anchor: والغرض أن ناشئة الليل هي: ساعاته وأوقاته، وكل ساعة منه تسمى ناشئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night prayer aligns heart and tongue and gathers attention for recitation, reflection, and understanding more than daytime prayer amid crowds, noise, and work.
rows.anchor: أشد مواطأة بين القلب واللسان، وأجمع على التلاوة

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas recited وأصوب قيلا in place of وأقوم قيلا.
rows.anchor: أن أنس بن مالك قرأ هذه الآية: "إن ناشئة الليل هي أشد وطئا وأصوب قيلا"

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas says أصوب, أقوم, أهيأ, and similar terms convey the same sense in this context.
rows.anchor: إن أصوب وأقوم وأهيأ وأشباه هذا واحد

words: إِنَّ لَكَ فِى ٱلنَّهَارِ سَبْحًۭا طَوِيلًۭا
rows.speaker: ابن عباس، وعكرمة، وعطاء بن أبي مسلم
rows.claim: They explain the long daytime span as free time and sleep.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، وعكرمة، وعطاء بن أبي مسلم: الفراغ والنوم

words: إِنَّ لَكَ فِى ٱلنَّهَارِ سَبْحًۭا طَوِيلًۭا
rows.speaker: أبو العالية، ومجاهد، وابن مالك، والضحاك، والحسن، وقتادة، والربيع بن أنس، وسفيان الثوري
rows.claim: These authorities explain سبحا طويلا as a long period of free time.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو العالية، ومجاهد، وابن مالك، والضحاك، والحسن، وقتادة، والربيع بن أنس، وسفيان الثوري: فراغا طويلا

words: إِنَّ لَكَ فِى ٱلنَّهَارِ سَبْحًۭا طَوِيلًۭا
rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada expands the meaning to free time, pursuit of needs, and movement from place to place.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: فراغا وبغية ومنقلبا

words: إِنَّ لَكَ فِى ٱلنَّهَارِ سَبْحًۭا طَوِيلًۭا
rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi interprets the phrase as abundant voluntary worship.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: {سبحا طويلا} تطوعا كثيرا

words: إِنَّ لَكَ فِى ٱلنَّهَارِ سَبْحًۭا طَوِيلًۭا
rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says attend to daytime needs and devote the night to religion; this applied when night prayer was obligatory, before 73:20 eased it, and Ibn Kathir endorses his account.
rows.anchor: قال: لحوائجك، فأفرغ لدينك الليل. قال: وهذا حين كانت صلاة الليل فريضة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن هشام
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Hisham planned to sell property for horses and weapons and fight the Romans until death; his townsmen recalled that the Prophet had forbidden six men who proposed the same.
rows.anchor: أنه طلق امرأته ثم ارتحل إلى المدينة ليبيع عقارا له بها ويجعله في الكراع والسلاح

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha describes the Prophet’s character as the Qur’an, then explains his night vigil in response to Sa'id’s question.
rows.anchor: قالت: فإن خلق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان القرآن

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that night vigil was initially obligatory; the Prophet and companions kept it for a year until their feet swelled, then the surah’s ending eased the duty to voluntary prayer. Ibn Kathir cites Ahmad’s full report and Muslim’s similar version.
rows.anchor: فإن الله افترض قيام الليل في أول هذه السورة، فقام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه حولا حتى انتفخت أقدامهم

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha describes eight night rak'ahs, sitting for remembrance and supplication at the eighth, then a ninth and two seated rak'ahs after the salutation.
rows.anchor: ثم يصلي ثماني ركعات لا يجلس فيهن إلا عند الثامنة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: As he aged, the Prophet prayed seven plus two seated rak'ahs; when sleep, pain, or illness kept him from night prayer, he prayed twelve by day, and did not recite the whole Qur'an in one night, stay up all night, or fast a full month outside Ramadan.
rows.anchor: فلما أسن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأخذه اللحم، أوتر بسبع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: After hearing Aisha’s account, Ibn Abbas affirmed it and said he would have visited her to hear it directly.
rows.anchor: فأتيت ابن عباس فحدثته بحديثها، فقال: صدقت، أما لو كنت أدخل عليها

words: أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ وَرَتِّلِ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ تَرْتِيلًا
rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: In another report Aisha says the Prophet came out displeased when people gathered to follow his night prayer, compassionately fearing that the vigil would become obligatory; he urged them to do only what they could sustain.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: كنت أجعل لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حصيرا يصلي عليه من الليل

words: أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ وَرَتِّلِ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ تَرْتِيلًا
rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha’s report says the people maintained the vigil intensely for eight months, after which God showed mercy, restored the obligatory prayers, and left night prayer voluntary; it also says the best deeds are those done consistently.
rows.anchor: وخير الأعمال ما ديم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says the route through Musa ibn Ubayda is weak, and the sound hadith omits the added claim that this surah was revealed then; the report’s wording may suggest a Medinan surah, but it is Meccan, and its eight-month interval conflicts with Ahmad’s year report.
rows.anchor: ورواه ابن أبي حاتم من طريق موسى بن عبيدة الربذي، وهو ضعيف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that people initially prayed roughly as much at night as in Ramadan, with close to a year between the surah’s beginning and end; several routes likewise report a year.
rows.anchor: سمعت ابن عباس يقول: أول ما نزل: أول المزمل، كانوا يقومون نحوا من قيامهم في شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
rows.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman says the believers kept night vigil for a year until their feet and shins swelled, then 73:20 brought relief; al-Hasan al-Basri agrees.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن قال: لما نزلت: {يا أيها المزمل}

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet and companions prayed until their feet swelled and that the surah’s ending was held in heaven for sixteen months before it descended.
rows.anchor: قالت: ألست تقرأ: {يا أيها المزمل}

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says they kept night vigil for a year or two until their legs and feet swelled, after which God sent relief at the end of the surah.
rows.anchor: وقال معمر، عن قتادة: {قم الليل إلا قليلا} قاموا حولا أو حولين

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the Prophet and a group of companions maintained the commanded vigil for ten years, until the final verse eased it.
rows.anchor: عن جعفر، عن سعيد -هو ابن جبير-قال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the command to the Prophet and believers to rise for most of the night burdened them, then 73:20 relieved and broadened the obligation.
rows.anchor: علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس

words: وَٱذْكُرِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remember God often, devote yourself to Him, and turn to worship when worldly tasks and needs are finished; Ibn Kathir connects this to 94:7 and cites Ibn Zayd in similar terms.
rows.anchor: أكثر من ذكره، وانقطع إليه، وتفرغ لعبادته إذا فرغت من أشغالك

words: وَٱذْكُرِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلًۭا
rows.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وأبو صالح، وعطية، والضحاك، والسدي
rows.claim: These authorities explain the command as making worship sincerely and exclusively for God.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومجاهد، وأبو صالح، وعطية، والضحاك، والسدي: {وتبتل إليه تبتيلا} أي: أخلص له العبادة

words: وَٱذْكُرِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلًۭا
rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the phrase as striving and devoting oneself to God.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: اجتهد وبتل إليه نفسك

words: وَٱذْكُرِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلًۭا
rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir notes that a worshipper is called a متبتل; the related hadith prohibition of تبتل means withdrawing to worship and abandoning marriage.
rows.anchor: يقال للعابد: متبتل، ومنه الحديث المروي: أنه نهى عن التبتل

words: رب المشرق والمغرب لا إله إلا هو فاتخذه وكيلا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns and governs east and west; as He alone is worshipped, He alone should be trusted, as also taught in 11:123 and 1:5.
rows.anchor: هو المالك المتصرف في المشارق والمغارب لا إله إلا هو

words: إن هذه تذكرة فمن شاء اتخذ إلى ربه سبيلا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is a reminder for people of understanding; a person’s taking a path to God depends on God’s willing to guide that person, as 76:30 makes explicit.
rows.anchor: يقول تعالى: {إن هذه} أي: السورة {تذكرة} أي: يتذكر بها أولو الألباب

words: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ تَقُومُ أَدْنَىٰ مِن ثُلُثَىِ ٱلَّيْلِ وَنِصْفَهُۥ وَثُلُثَهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet and some companions varied between these portions without aiming at exact fractions, because maintaining the prescribed vigil was difficult.
rows.anchor: تارة هكذا، وتارة هكذا، وذلك كله من غير قصد منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God measures the night and day so they sometimes match and sometimes one lengthens at the expense of the other.
rows.anchor: تارة يعتدلان، وتارة يأخذ هذا من هذا، أو هذا من هذا

words: عَلِمَ أَن لَّن تُحْصُوهُ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knew the believers could not keep exact count of the required night portion, so He eased the duty and allowed whatever recitation is manageable, meaning night prayer without a fixed duration.
rows.anchor: علم أن لن تحصوه} أي: الفرض الذي أوجبه عليكم {فاقرءوا ما تيسر من القرآن}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recitation here stands for prayer, as in 17:110, where not raising one’s voice in prayer means not raising it in recitation.
rows.anchor: كما قال في سورة سبحان: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك}

rows.speaker: أصحاب الإمام أبي حنيفة
rows.claim: Hanafi jurists use this verse and the report telling a poor-performing worshipper to read what is easy to argue that al-Fatiha is not required and even one verse suffices.
rows.anchor: استدل أصحاب الإمام أبي حنيفة، رحمه الله، بهذه الآية

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority answer that position with the Prophet’s statement that prayer is invalid without the Opening of the Book, reinforced by reports requiring Umm al-Kitab in every prayer.
rows.anchor: أجابهم الجمهور بحديث عبادة بن الصامت

words: عَلِمَ أَن سَيَكُونُ مِنكُم مَّرْضَىٰ وَءَاخَرُونَ يَضْرِبُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ يَبْتَغُونَ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God foreknows that illness, travel for livelihood, and fighting in His path will excuse some Muslims from night vigil; since this Meccan surah preceded legislation of fighting, the prediction is a sign of prophethood.
rows.anchor: مكية، ولم يكن القتال شرع بعد، فهي من أكبر دلائل النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated instruction means to perform as much night prayer as is manageable.
rows.anchor: أي: قوموا بما تيسر عليكم منه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan condemns a memorizer who prays only the obligatory prayers as one who neglects the Qur'an, and says a little night recitation, even five verses, is required of its bearers.
rows.anchor: قال: يتوسد القرآن، لعن الله ذاك، قال الله تعالى للعبد الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says that one who sleeps until morning has Satan urinate in his ear; commentators differ whether this means missing an obligatory prayer or night vigil.
rows.anchor: فقيل معناه: نام عن المكتوبة. وقيل: عن قيام الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two hadiths urge the people of Qur'an to pray witr, one saying to do so and another warning that whoever omits witr is not of the community.
rows.anchor: وفي السنن: "أوتروا يا أهل القرآن."

rows.speaker: أبو بكر عبد العزيز
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir notes as an unusually strong position Abu Bakr Abd al-Aziz’s view that Ramadan night vigil is obligatory, adding that God knows best.
rows.anchor: وأغرب من هذا ما حكي عن أبي بكر عبد العزيز، من الحنابلة، من إيجابه قيام شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet through Ibn Abbas interprets the manageable recitation as one hundred verses; Ibn Kathir later calls this report very strange and says he found it only in al-Tabarani’s collection.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: {فاقرءوا ما تيسر منه}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the hundred-verse report very strange and says he found it only in al-Tabarani’s Mu'jam.
rows.anchor: وهذا حديث غريب جدا لم أره إلا في معجم الطبراني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse commands the obligatory prayer and zakah; this indicates zakah was prescribed in Mecca, while its thresholds and payment details were specified in Medina.
rows.anchor: مقادير النصب والمخرج لم تبين إلا بالمدينة

words: عَلِمَ أَن لَّن تُحْصُوهُ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس، وعكرمة، ومجاهد، والحسن، وقتادة
rows.claim: These early authorities say the final verse abrogated the original obligation of night vigil; reports differ on how long that first obligation lasted.
rows.anchor: إن هذه الآية نسخت الذي كان الله قد أوجبه على المسلمين

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In the Sahihayn, the Prophet tells a questioner that five daily prayers are required and there is no other obligation unless one volunteers.
rows.anchor: ثبت في الصحيحين أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لذلك الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lending God a good loan means giving charity, for which God grants the best and most abundant reward; Ibn Kathir links this to 2:245.
rows.anchor: يعني: من الصدقات، فإن الله يجازي على ذلك أحسن الجزاء وأوفره

words: وَمَا تُقَدِّمُوا۟ لِأَنفُسِكُم مِّنْ خَيْرٍۢ تَجِدُوهُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever good people send ahead will be preserved with God and is better than what they keep for themselves in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وهو خير مما أبقيتموه لأنفسكم في الدنيا

words: وَمَا تُقَدِّمُوا۟ لِأَنفُسِكُم مِّنْ خَيْرٍۢ تَجِدُوهُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: The Prophet contrasts wealth sent ahead with wealth left to heirs: a person’s real wealth is what they have given or prepared for the afterlife, while the heir receives what was deferred.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seek God’s forgiveness often in every affair, since He forgives and shows mercy to those who ask.
rows.anchor: أكثروا من ذكره واستغفاره في أموركم كلها

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: A report in Sahih al-Bukhari has Jabir say the first Qur'an revealed was 74:1; most scholars instead identify 96:1 as the first revelation.
rows.anchor: عن جابر أنه كان يقول: أول شيء نزل من القرآن

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir recounts that after his retreat at Hira, the Prophet heard a call, saw something, returned to Khadijah asking to be covered and doused with cold water, and then 74:1–3 descended.
rows.anchor: فرفعت رأسي فرأيت شيئا، فأتيت خديجة فقلت: دثروني. وصبوا علي ماء باردا

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: In Muslim’s version Jabir places the angel on a throne between heaven and earth after a pause in revelation; Ibn Kathir calls this the preserved account, which proves revelation preceded this surah, and reconciles the reports by saying 74 was first after the pause.
rows.anchor: فإذا الملك الذي جاءني بحراء قاعد على كرسي بين السماء والأرض

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir’s account through Ahmad and the two Sahih collections says that after the pause the Prophet saw the angel, was overcome by fear, asked to be wrapped, and received 74:1–5 as revelation resumed.
rows.anchor: ثم فتر الوحي عني فترة، فبينا أنا أمشي سمعت صوتا من السماء، فرفعت بصري

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that after Quraysh debated whether Muhammad was a sorcerer, soothsayer, or poet and settled on transmitted magic, the Prophet grieved and covered his head; then 74:1–7 descended.
rows.anchor: سمعت ابن عباس يقول: إن الوليد بن المغيرة صنع لقريش طعاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to brace for action and warn the people; with this command the Prophet’s messengerhood was established, just as the first revelation established his prophethood.
rows.anchor: شمر عن ساق العزم، وأنذر الناس. وبهذا حصل الإرسال، كما حصل بالأول النبوة
